chapters.n: Here Mormon, the main editor of the Book of Mormon, steps in—writing about AD 385, centuries after the surrounding chapters. He is about to give his record to his son Moroni and has witnessed nearly all his people’s destruction.
Mormon expects Moroni to see the Nephites’ total destruction. He prays Moroni survives to write about them and about Christ, hoping it may someday help their descendants.
After abridging the large plates up to King Benjamin, Mormon found the small plates of Nephi among his records—containing the prophets from Jacob to Benjamin and much of Nephi.
He loved these plates because of their prophecies of Christ. Many have been fulfilled, and Mormon is sure the rest will be.
He chose to complete his record using the large plates for the rest of the history. He can’t record even a hundredth of his people’s story.
Mormon will include the small plates with his abridgment because they are precious to him and will be to his people.

He does this “for a wise purpose” prompted by the Spirit, though he doesn’t know why. Latter-day Saints see the reason in 1828: when 116 manuscript pages of Mormon’s abridgment were lost, the small plates covered the same period.

f.w: I do not know all things

chapters.n: He prays his people’s descendants will once again know God and Christ’s redemption and be a delightsome people.
Mormon continues his abridgment from the plates of Nephi as God enables him.
King Benjamin placed the small plates with the royal records handed down by the kings.
These records passed down from Benjamin until they reached Mormon. He is certain they will be preserved, because people will be judged by them at the last day.
Mormon now bridges back to the story. King Benjamin faced some internal conflict.
Lamanite armies invaded. Benjamin led his armies personally, fighting with the sword of Laban.
With the Lord’s strength they defeated many thousands and drove the Lamanites out of their lands.

f.w: in the strength of the Lord

chapters.n: False Christs arose but were silenced and punished for their crimes.
False prophets and teachers were also punished, and many dissenters defected to the Lamanites. Then Benjamin, aided by holy prophets…

f.g: Nephites who abandoned their people and joined the Lamanites, often stirring up war.

chapters.n: Benjamin was a holy and righteous king. Many holy men spoke God’s word with power and sharpness because the people were stubborn.
With their help, and by laboring with all his body and soul, King Benjamin reestablished peace—setting the stage for his great sermon in Mosiah 2–5.
